topic: Antennas, feed lines and SWR (T9, T7C)

questions.question: Which of the following might be the cause of low RF power output from a solid-state transceiver?

choices.D: High SWR

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a dummy load?

choices.A: To prevent transmitting signals over the air when making tests
choices.B: To prevent over-modulation of a transmitter
choices.C: To improve the efficiency of an antenna
choices.D: To improve the signal-to-noise ratio of a receiver

questions.answer: To prevent transmitting signals over the air when making tests

questions.question: Which of the following is used to determine if an antenna is resonant at the desired operating frequency?

choices.D: A frequency counter

questions.question: What does a typical RF dummy load consist of?

choices.A: A low-voltage power supply and an AC relay
choices.B: A 50-ohm non-inductive resistor mounted on a heat sink
choices.C: A low-voltage power supply and a DC relay
choices.D: A 50-ohm inductive reactance mounted in a shielded enclosure

questions.answer: A 50-ohm non-inductive resistor mounted on a heat sink

questions.question: What reading on an SWR meter indicates a perfect impedance match between the antenna and the feed line?

choices.D: Full Scale

questions.question: Why do most solid-state transmitters reduce output power as SWR increases beyond a certain level?

choices.A: To protect the RF output amplifier transistors
choices.B: To comply with FCC rules on spectral purity
choices.C: Because power supplies cannot supply enough current at high SWR
choices.D: To lower the SWR on the transmission line

questions.answer: To protect the RF output amplifier transistors

questions.question: What does an SWR reading of 4:1 indicate?

choices.D: Impedance mismatch

questions.question: What happens to power lost in a feed line?

choices.D: It distorts the signal

questions.question: Which instrument can be used to determine SWR?

choices.D: Directional wattmeter

questions.question: Which of the following causes failure of coaxial cables?

choices.C: Rapid fluctuation in transmitter output power
choices.D: Operation at 100% duty cycle for an extended period

questions.question: Why should the outer jacket of coaxial cable be resistant to ultraviolet light?

choices.A: Ultraviolet light can increase the resistance of the conductors
choices.B: Ultraviolet light can increase losses in the cable’s jacket
choices.C: Ultraviolet and RF signals can mix, causing interference
choices.D: Ultraviolet light can damage the jacket and allow water to enter the cable

questions.answer: Ultraviolet light can damage the jacket and allow water to enter the cable

questions.question: What is an advantage of foam-dielectric versus solid-dielectric coaxial cable?

choices.A: It is more resistant to moisture contamination
choices.C: It has less loss per foot
choices.D: It has a better impedance match to 50 ohms

questions.answer: It has less loss per foot

questions.question: What is a beam antenna?

choices.A: An antenna built from square aluminum beams
choices.B: An omnidirectional antenna invented by Clarence Beam
choices.C: An antenna that concentrates signals in one direction
choices.D: An antenna that focuses the signal into two intense rays

questions.answer: An antenna that concentrates signals in one direction

questions.question: Which of the following describes a type of antenna loading?

choices.A: Electrically lengthening by inserting inductors in radiating elements
choices.B: Inserting a resistor in the radiating portion of the antenna to make it resonant
choices.C: Installing a spring in the base of a mobile vertical antenna to make it more flexible
choices.D: Strengthening the radiating elements of a beam antenna to better resist wind damage

questions.answer: Electrically lengthening by inserting inductors in radiating elements

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of a handheld radio transceiver’s short flexible antenna compared to a full-sized quarter-wave antenna?

choices.B: It transmits only circularly polarized signals
choices.C: It is more susceptible to receiver desensitization
choices.D: It only works on analog signals, not digital ones

questions.question: Which of the following increases the resonant frequency of a dipole antenna?

choices.B: Inserting coils in series with radiating wires
choices.D: Adding capacitive loading to the ends of the radiating wires

questions.question: Which of the following types of antennas offers the greatest gain?

choices.D: Yagi

questions.question: What is a potential drawback of using a handheld VHF transceiver inside a vehicle that lacks an externally mounted antenna?

choices.A: Signal strength is reduced due to the shielding effect of the vehicle
choices.B: The bandwidth of the antenna will decrease, increasing SWR
choices.C: The SWR might decrease, decreasing the signal strength
choices.D: The handheld will overheat due to reflected power in the vehicle

questions.answer: Signal strength is reduced due to the shielding effect of the vehicle

questions.question: Why is a 19-inch-long vertical antenna often used on 2 meters?

choices.D: It has low RF radiation exposure

questions.question: What is an advantage of a 5/8-wavelength whip antenna for VHF or UHF mobile service compared to a 1/4-wave antenna?

choices.B: It radiates at a higher angle
choices.D: It has lower impedance

questions.question: In which direction does a half-wave dipole antenna radiate the strongest signal?

choices.B: Off the ends of the antenna
choices.C: In the direction of the feed line
choices.D: Broadside to the antenna

questions.question: What is antenna gain?

choices.A: The additional power that is added to the transmitter power
choices.B: The additional power that is required in the antenna when transmitting on a higher frequency
choices.C: The increase in signal strength in a specified direction compared to a reference antenna
choices.D: The increase in impedance on receive or transmit compared to a reference antenna

questions.answer: The increase in signal strength in a specified direction compared to a reference antenna

questions.question: Which of the following connectors should be carefully taped for weather protection when used outdoors?

choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.question: What is the most common impedance of coaxial cables used in amateur radio?

choices.D: 12 ohms

questions.question: Why is coaxial cable the most common feed line for amateur radio antenna systems?

choices.A: It is easy to use and requires few special installation considerations
choices.B: It has less loss than any other type of feed line
choices.C: It can handle more power than any other type of feed line
choices.D: It is less expensive than any other type of feed line

questions.answer: It is easy to use and requires few special installation considerations

questions.question: What is the major function of an antenna tuner (antenna coupler)?

choices.A: It matches the antenna system impedance to the transceiver's output impedance
choices.B: It helps a receiver automatically tune in weak stations
choices.C: It allows an antenna to be used on both transmit and receive
choices.D: It automatically selects the proper antenna for the frequency band being used

questions.answer: It matches the antenna system impedance to the transceiver's output impedance

questions.question: What happens as the frequency of a signal in coaxial cable is increased?

choices.D: The loss increases

questions.question: Which of the following connector types is most suitable as an RF connector for frequencies above 400 MHz?

choices.D: DB-25

questions.question: Which of the following is true of PL-259 type coax connectors?

choices.A: They are preferred for microwave operation
choices.C: They are commonly used at HF and VHF frequencies
choices.D: They are a bayonet-type connector

questions.answer: They are commonly used at HF and VHF frequencies

questions.question: Which of the following is a source of loss in coaxial feed line?

choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.question: What can cause erratic changes in SWR?

choices.B: Loose connection in the antenna or feed line
choices.D: Overload from a strong local station

questions.answer: Loose connection in the antenna or feed line

questions.question: What is the electrical difference between RG-58 and RG-213 coaxial cable?

choices.A: There is no significant difference between the two types
choices.C: RG-213 cable has less loss at a given frequency
choices.D: RG-58 cable can handle higher power levels

questions.answer: RG-213 cable has less loss at a given frequency

questions.question: Which of the following types of feed line has the lowest loss?

choices.D: 75-ohm flexible coax

questions.question: What is standing wave ratio (SWR)?

choices.A: A measure of how well a load is matched to a transmission line
choices.B: The ratio of amplifier power output to input
choices.D: An indication of the quality of your station’s ground connection

questions.answer: A measure of how well a load is matched to a transmission line
